name: GM - Marion Metal Center, Marion IN

fieldNotes.site: GM Marion Metal Center, 2400 W 2nd St, Marion (Grant County) IN 46952 - an active GM metal-stamping plant founded 1956 as Fisher Body, ~750+ employees, producing steel/aluminum blanks, stampings and sub-assemblies (doors, hoods, deck lids, quarter panels, Tahoe/Suburban roof panels) for GM assembly plants across North America. GM announced a $491M investment to retool for EV stampings (plus a prior $91M/$90M upgrade). Roster address geocodes onto W 2nd St in a residential block ~1.5 km east of the actual plant; the correct plant center is 40.56381,-85.69851 (from Mapcarta/GM Authority and confirmed by satellite as the large multi-roof stamping building fronting W 2nd St, bounded on the north by the rail line and on the east by a residential street).
fieldNotes.truckGate: Confirmed - chain-link perimeter fencing rings the entire property on every street-view frame (W 2nd St south frontage, the east residential-street frontage, and the west/SW frontage). Multiple controlled truck entrances: the primary SW truck/rail drive off W 2nd St, plus perimeter gates on the east side serving the trailer/material yard. truckGateCount estimated 3 (front employee/visitor + SW freight/rail drive + east yard gate).
fieldNotes.guardShack: Marked true at medium confidence - a fenced active GM stamping plant of this scale (750+ employees, JIT stamping shipments to multiple assembly plants) conventionally runs a staffed gatehouse at the freight entrance. Small structures sit beside the entrances but a guard booth could not be individually resolved from overhead; flagged uncertain along with remoteGs.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: Marked false - no dedicated paved truck-waiting apron outside the gates was identified; the W 2nd St frontage is grass setback to the fence line.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: True - the large internal paved yards (west truck drive and the east material/trailer yard) give ample post-gate holding/queue room before docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: True - internal drives from each gate to the docks/yards are long and deep, easily holding 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: True - very wide paved truck drives and gate aprons (SW drive and east yard) have unused width to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimated 25-50 dock doors distributed across the west and north/NW building faces serving the rail-side laydown and the inbound material drive; exact count partly obscured by roof overhang - flagged uncertain. dockDoorCount ~30.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer parking and outdoor steel-coil/stamping-stock racking fill the east yard in long rows, plus trailers along the west drive; banded 25-50 (capacity well over 50 if the large empty SE paved lot is counted). dropYard true. trailersVisible ~35.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: True - inbound steel/material handling and rail are concentrated on the west/NW side (rail spurs + coil racks), while finished-stamping trailer shipping uses the east material/trailer yard; two physically separate freight clusters on different building faces.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed rail-served - multiple rail spurs branch off the mainline on the north property edge and curve into the west/NW side of the plant serving the inbound steel laydown; visible in the NW and west satellite crops.
fieldNotes.scale: Possible truck scale near the SW/west freight drive but not positively resolved - flagged uncertain, left false.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: False - one very large interconnected multi-roof stamping building; buildingCount 1.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Marion is a small Indiana city; the plant sits at the western edge of town with farm fields immediately west and south and only a residential strip to the east - judged Rural per rubric (small-town/edge-of-town industrial).
